# SciFact within-abstract position prior screen

## Question and sources

Does a query-independent sentence-position prior estimated from SciFact annotations improve evidence ranking in a known cited abstract over tuned lexical matching and matched position heuristics? The preceding sentence study tested lexical scores from neighboring sentences. This follow-up tests the sentence index. Both studies use the official SciFact **training** release for internal development. This screen may share instances with earlier studies and is not independent confirmation. Leave the official development and test members unopened.

Use the corpus and training members of the archive pinned to SHA-256 `11c621288d41ac144d29b13b0f8503b3820b7d6e8b1f6ff24dff335c196d76be`. Include every training claim–document pair with at least one annotated evidence sentence, pooling support and refutation. The candidates are every sentence in the supplied abstract. Gold is the union of annotated sentence indices for the pair. Exclude rows without any evidence from scoring, but use all published training citations and evidence document IDs to construct source components.

## Document-disjoint development

Connect all sources linked by any training claim using the union of its cited and evidence document IDs. For each connected component, join its numerically sorted IDs with commas and hash the UTF-8 string with SHA-256. Interpret the first eight bytes as an unsigned big-endian integer, modulo 4. Buckets 0 and 1 fit the prior, bucket 2 selects settings, and bucket 3 screens the locked methods. All claims and all documents belong to at most one partition. Use the screen labels exclusively for the final evaluation. After selection, refit only the prior on the combined fit and selection pairs.

## Scores and controls

Compute lexical statistics separately within each abstract. Compare English-stopword word unigram/bigram TF-IDF cosine (as in the earlier sentence study), character-within-word 3–5 gram TF-IDF cosine and positive-IDF BM25 (distinct lowercased word tokens in the claim). Tune BM25 over k1 in {.6, 1.2, 1.8} and b in {.25, .75}. Each signal divides scores within each pair by its own maximum; an all-zero signal stays zero. The strong lexical comparator takes a convex combination of these three normalized signals on the .25-spaced simplex, including the standalone signals. Choose BM25 settings first using standalone BM25. Then choose the lexical mixture using the selected BM25. Use the same frozen mixture for all augmented methods. Select by pair-mean MRR with deterministic ties to smaller k1 then b for BM25 and larger BM25 then word weight for the mixture.

For each candidate sentence with zero-based index i in an abstract of length n, use bin floor(5 × (i + .5) / n). Fit gold and non-gold counts by bin, with one pseudo-count per outcome. A sentence contributes once per pair. The learned score for a bin is log((gold + 1) / (non-gold + 1)). For each abstract, center the scores on their within-abstract mean. Add lambda times that centered vector to the common lexical score. Compare against three matched controls. Keep exactly the same multiset of offsets per abstract, but assign them in strictly nondecreasing order of sentence index (later-first) or nonincreasing order (earlier-first), or assign the increasing offsets by the ascending SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string `position-control:<doc_id>:<index>` (hash order, ties by index). The same document receives the same placement for all claims. For each of the four augmented methods independently select lambda from {0, .05, .10, .20, .40, .80} by selection MRR with the lower weight winning ties. Also report standalone word TF-IDF, character TF-IDF, tuned BM25, learned position-only ranking and strict earlier-first and later-first position-only rankings. All rank ties favor the lower sentence index.

## Outcomes and decision

Primary endpoint is mean pair reciprocal rank of the first annotated sentence. Secondary endpoint is mean pair recall@3, the fraction of the pair's distinct annotated indices in the first three ranks. Report both endpoints for every method. Report paired candidate-minus-control differences for MRR and recall@3 against the common lexical comparator and the three matched augmented controls. Use a bootstrap of 10,000 resamples of whole screen source components with replacement (NumPy default_rng, seed 20261121, components ordered by numeric ID tuples), jointly retaining all associated pairs in each draw and using pair-weighted ratios. Use Bonferroni-adjusted percentile intervals across the four primary contrasts at familywise 95%. Report unadjusted 95% intervals for the secondary contrasts as descriptive. The screen favors the learned augmentation only if all four simultaneous primary lower bounds are above zero. Save per-pair screen rankings, selection scores, fitted position counts and aggregate results without any source text.

The evaluation supplies the cited abstract, conditions on the selected settings and fitted prior, and addresses only annotated sentence ranking. It does not estimate performance on untouched data, complete rationale recovery, stance classification or open retrieval.
